A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3H model-merging study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are accessible and support reliable comparison across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original DPO-training and model-merging experiments on Llama3 and Mistral, including static and continual evaluations, ablations, and seed/sparsity studies.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, mechanism diagnostics, pruning comparisons, and continual-setting results for RESM.

M1.justification: RESM retains R-TSVM's outlier-weighting and SVD framework, but substantially revises rank allocation. V1 Eq. (10) uses floor(d_l(1-gamma*Omega_l)); v3 Eq. (9) and Algorithm 1 use floor(d_l(gamma0+gamma*Omega_l)). This introduces a base-rank parameter and reverses how sparsity affects retained rank.

E1.justification: Both use the same ten preference datasets, five annotation perspectives, eleven evaluation benchmarks, and static/continual 3H tasks. The added model-count sweep changes configurations within retained coverage rather than introducing a new task or data domain.

E2.justification: V3 Table 5 adds evaluated TSVM+Wanda and TSVM+Owl comparators against RESM. The existing data-mixture and model-merging comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: V3 replaces the principal aggregate AVG score with the mean relative gain across the three dimensions against each Instruct backbone, changing comparative scoring throughout the results. Figure 2 also introduces a 3/6/9/12-model sweep and a 95%-singular-value-energy rank diagnostic. Existing training budgets, backbones, and judge-evaluation sample counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 Figure 2 adds studies of outlier weighting as the number of merged models increases and of the ranks needed by sparse versus dense layers to retain 95% energy. These substantially extend the mechanism-focused analyses. V1's component ablations and seed/sparsity sensitivity studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain the seed 0–3 sensitivity study, shown in v1 Figure 3 and v3 Figure 5. V3 introduces no new repeated-run reporting practice, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds RESM continual results, pruning-comparison results, and Figure 2 findings. Reported Llama3 static helpfulness/honesty changes from 59.72/57.20 to 59.62/58.20; most baseline task scores remain unchanged. Aggregates are replaced by normalized gains, so these are not controlled version-to-version improvements. The Mistral Stage 3 MMLU entry, 60.51 in v1, is blank in v3 Table 11.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 revises the sparsity-dependent conflict bound and adds random-unit-vector assumptions, a cosine-threshold conflict definition, and a concentration-based proof absent from v1. V1's explicit weight-concentration inequality is removed. These are substantive mathematical changes, independently of the method rename.

C1.justification: The benchmark, 3H trade-off findings, and model-merging contribution remain central. V3 specifically claims to address preference-noise accumulation and adds quantified gain ranges in the abstract, extending v1's emphasis on enhancing TSVM through heavy-tail and sparsity awareness.

C2.justification: V3 interprets growing weighting benefits with more merged models as preference-noise accumulation and distinguishes merging-time conflict handling from post-hoc pruning. It also expands the rationale for excluding adaptation-based merging. The helpfulness limitation and inter-/intra-dimension conflict discussion are retained, moving from v1 Section 5.3 to v3 Appendix D.

D1.justification: V3 supplies defaults gamma0=0.2 and gamma=0.6 for the revised rank rule; existing training, hardware, and evaluation details remain largely unchanged. Its abstract now states that models are released, although Appendix C.1 still promises release upon acceptance, leaving actual availability unresolved within the PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning around preference noise, localized alignment behavior, adaptive merging, and outlier-based pruning. New Appendix B.3 and expanded B.2 distinguish RESM from single-model pruning and test-time adaptation, beyond v1's alignment-tax and MoE discussions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method review, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. V3 presents motivation and the proposed method before the experiments, replacing v1's benchmark-first, extended-method-study structure. It also renames R-TSVM to RESM and reorganizes appendix sections.

P2.justification: V3 changes the main text from two columns to predominantly one column, adds conceptual and diagnostic figures, and redesigns result tables with colored relative-gain annotations. Detailed proposed-method static results are integrated into the main comparisons, while the Llama3 continual table moves to the appendix. Existing sensitivity plots are relocated and relabeled.

improvement.justification: V3 resolves the mismatch between v1's rank formula and its stated sparse-layer behavior, while new diagnostic, pruning, and continual evaluations strengthen empirical support. The gains are limited by unresolved theoretical validity: the added Appendix A.2 proof equates a fixed-threshold probability with a tail integral and contains an invalid bounding step, so it does not establish the advertised guarantee.
